cohort: All deliveries in Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden between 2000 and 2011
finding: The increased total cesarean rates in the Nordic countries are primarily attributed to increased rates among nulliparous women and women with previous cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: The study found that increases in cesarean rates in Nordic countries were primarily driven by increases in cesarean deliveries among nulliparous women and women with previous cesareans.
